assumptions: USD million unless explicitly local currency (LC). Fictional North Lantern group. Toy foreign subsidiary translation uses average FX for annual profit, closing FX for assets/liabilities, historical rate for capital contributions; translation residual OCI. Subsidiary wholly owned.

evidence.text: [Local balance, LC million] Opening assets 500, liabilities 200, net assets 300. Closing assets 610, liabilities 240, net assets 370. No acquisition or disposal.

[Local P&L] Revenue 420, operating expense 320, interest 20, tax 20, profit 60. Dividend 10 LC paid midyear. New capital contribution 20 LC paid midyear by parent. Net asset roll-forward 300+60−10+20=370.
[FX schedule] Opening USD/LC 0.80, average 0.75, closing 0.70. Dividend date 0.78, contribution date 0.76. No other rates required.

[Policy] Translate subsidiary net assets at closing; opening translated net assets from prior closing FX; profit average; dividend and contribution transaction rate; residual translation adjustment to OCI. Group consolidation eliminates parent's investment and subsidiary intragroup dividend/contribution.
[Parent P&L] External revenue 500 USD, expenses including tax 420 USD; excludes subsidiary and internal dividends. No intercompany trading.
[Cash note] Subsidiary ending cash 50 LC included in assets. Parent receives dividend internally; no external shareholder distribution or sale of subsidiary.
[Presentation] CFO reports difference between closing translated net assets and opening translated net assets as net profit; uses closing FX on annual subsidiary sales.

qas.question: Translate the subsidiary's annual revenue at the rate prescribed for flows.
Find subsidiary translated annual profit for consolidation.
Determine translated closing net assets from the local balance sheet.
Calculate the translation residual in OCI using the disclosed net asset bridge.
qas.answer: Opening 240; profit 45; dividend −7.8; contribution +15.2; pre-translation 292.4; OCI=259−292.4=−33.4 million USD.

qas.question: Find consolidated external revenue for the year.
Explain why the 19m increase in translated net assets is not subsidiary profit.
qas.answer: The change combines profit, dividend, capital contribution and negative translation OCI; translated profit is 45m. Ending balance difference alone does not measure performance.

qas.question: Does the parent's receipt of 7.8m translated dividend increase consolidated external cash?
qas.answer: No. The transfer is intragroup; it changes the location of group cash, not total external cash.

qas.question: Can exchange-rate effect on the group's consolidated cash flow be calculated from this information?
qas.answer: No. Opening subsidiary cash, dated cash movements, and cash-flow translation rates are missing.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional marketplace Briar Basket sells owned inventory as principal and operates third-party marketplace as agent; payment processing gross cash collected on behalf of sellers is not revenue. No tax.

evidence.text: [Orders] Own-inventory gross sales 300m including 20m returns/refunds; owned-goods revenue net 280. Third-party merchant GMV 500 excluding cancelled orders; platform earns commission 12% of verified GMV. Merchant goods are never controlled by platform.
[Payments] Platform collects 500m cash for merchants, pays 400m cash to them during year. Commission withheld from settlement. Opening merchant payable 15m. No other merchant fees or refunds.
[Owned-goods cost] COGS 170m net of returned inventory; fulfillment cost 35m on own sales only. Marketplace processing/support cost 28m. Common overhead 40m, no depreciation beyond these expenses.
[Other service] Advertising to third-party merchants earned 25m, separately invoiced. Cash collected 20m, opening ad AR 3m. Ad cost 5m, not included in common costs.
[KPI definition] GMV is net own merchandise transaction value plus third-party GMV, excludes advertising. Take rate equals third-party commission/third-party GMV, excludes ads.
[Draft] Management reports 805m revenue (280+500+25), deducts seller remittances as marketplace COGS; also adds withheld commission as other revenue.
[Cash disclosure] Own customers paid net 280m. All operating costs paid. No other cash flows or AR.

qas.question: Find recognized marketplace commission, separating seller GMV from platform consideration.
Reconcile the closing merchant payable using GMV collected, withheld commission and seller payments.
Determine total recognized platform revenue including own goods and advertising.
Calculate consolidated operating result on the correct gross/net presentation.
Reconcile closing advertising receivable without mixing seller settlement liabilities.
Explain why both grossing up seller GMV and adding the commission to it would misstate the economics.
qas.answer: The platform is an agent on third-party goods, so commission is the earned consideration; seller funds are a payable. Adding the fee to gross GMV counts part of the same customer payment twice.

qas.question: Would taking 60/805 give the specified take rate?
qas.answer: No. The defined base is third-party GMV 500, not misclassified revenue or total GMV. Take rate is 12%.

qas.question: Can the profit of third-party merchants be derived from seller remittances 400?
qas.answer: No. Settlement cash is not merchant revenue or profit; merchant cost and opening balances are not supplied.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional Reed Bridge bank. Toy capital ratio uses stated deductions and RWA; approved year-end regulatory capital excludes proposed distributions only if specified. Actual vs stress explicitly separate.

evidence.text: [Audited equity bridge] Opening common equity 950m; annual profit attributable common 110m; dividends paid 45m; OCI loss 25m; new common issuance 60m. No other common movements.

[Regulatory reconciliation] At year-end goodwill 80m, other intangible deduction 25m, disallowed DTA 15m, prudent valuation adjustment 5m. CET1 before planned distribution = common equity less all deductions. RWA credit 6,800m, market 500m, operational 700m.
[Board minutes Jan next year] Proposed 40m dividend not approved at reporting date. Toy capital policy nevertheless deducts it in forward-looking capital plan only, not actual year-end CET1.

[Stress pack] Additional after-tax credit loss 90m decreases CET1; RWA credit increases 500m, market/operational unchanged. No change in deductions or OCI. Planned dividend assumed paid in stress unless cancelled.
[Capital limits] Toy minimum CET1 ratio 10.5%; management buffer target 12%. No new issuance in stress.
[Deck] Management reports year-end common equity/RWA as CET1 and says stress ratio is unchanged because loss is noncash.
[Disclosure] No Tier 2 capital, leverage exposure, applicable real-world jurisdiction or approval outcome.

qas.question: Reconcile actual closing common equity from the audited bridge.
Find actual year-end CET1 after regulatory deductions, without the forward dividend.
Calculate actual CET1 ratio against total disclosed RWA.
Compute stress CET1 ratio after both credit loss and planned dividend.
How much additional CET1 would be needed to reach 10.5% after stress if dividend is cancelled?
Why is common equity divided by RWA not the stipulated regulatory ratio?
qas.answer: The denominator alone is not enough; the numerator requires deductions 125m. Equity ratio would overstate CET1.

qas.question: Does cancelling the proposed dividend alone restore compliance under stress?
qas.answer: No. Stress capital 835m against required 892.5m remains insufficient by 57.5m.

qas.question: Can the actual legal capital distribution restriction be established?
qas.answer: No. The thresholds and treatment are fictional, and the real jurisdiction, buffers and other capital measures are not supplied.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional insurer Cedar Cove. Toy savings portfolio interest credit based on opening account balance; maturity/reinvestment cash affects next year's investment income, not this year's accrued returns. No mortality or tax.

evidence.text: [Policy account] Opening account liability 800m; new deposits 120m, withdrawals 100m. Guaranteed crediting rate 3.5% opening liability; credited amount increases account obligation. No other change.

[Investments current year] Opening assets supporting portfolio 850m: 500m bonds at 5%, 350m at 4%. Full-year income on opening assets only. All interest collected. Asset principal unchanged before net investment purchases.
[Cash] Deposits and withdrawals fund net principal investment 20m at year-end; new investment yields 3% next year. Interest credited not paid. Admin cost 8m cash.
[Maturity note] 200m of 5% bonds mature at next Jan1 and are immediately reinvested at 2.5%; remaining rates unchanged. No asset principal loss or other changes in next-year scenario.
[Forecast convention] Next-year guarantee applied to closing current liability; no new deposits/withdrawals next year for simple sensitivity. Admin cost remains 8.
[Investor deck] Claims current asset portfolio average 4.59% means guaranteed spread remains constant forever; treats new deposits as premium revenue.
[Risk] No option behavior, surrender charges, duration, market value or future rates beyond scenario.

qas.question: Calculate credited interest and closing account liability for the current year.
Find current-year recurring investment interest from the opening portfolio.
Find current savings-portfolio profit after credited interest and admin.
Find next-year investment income under the reinvestment scenario.
Determine next-year profit sensitivity with the closing guarantee base.
Why can lower reinvestment yields squeeze profit even though existing bonds still pay fixed coupons?
qas.answer: Maturing high-yield assets are replaced by lower-yield assets, while credited interest applies to the larger liability base; both effects reduce the spread.

qas.question: Should the 120m new deposits be recognized as earned insurance revenue in this case?
qas.answer: No. They increase repayable account liabilities; the model has no separate insurance service consideration.

qas.question: Can the policy portfolio's economic solvency under a full yield-curve shock be established?
qas.answer: No. Asset/liability duration, market valuations and policy behavior are not supplied.

assumptions: USD million; million usage units. Fictional cloud company Quartz Loop. Toy contract allocates minimum commitment to service units and a distinct onboarding service. Unused minimum only recognized upon expiry; excess usage charged separately.

evidence.text: [Contract P] Annual minimum cash prepaid 24m: onboarding allocation 4m (accepted Jan1), 20m usage credits at $1/unit for 20m units. Credits expire December 31, no rollover/refund.
[Usage P] Metered consumption 16m units before year-end, 4m credits expire confirmed. Direct serving cost $.55 per used unit; onboarding cost 2m.

[Contract Q] Quarterly billing in arrears, no minimum. Consumes 10m units at $1.20/unit, including 2m in December not yet invoiced but unconditional billing right. Cash paid 9m, opening AR 1m, no writeoffs.
[Service Q] Direct serving cost $.70/unit. Shared infrastructure cash expense 5m. All costs paid. No tax, other products or capex.
[Accounting] Usage revenue only as units consumed or qualifying expired credits; Q December unbilled unconditional right included AR. Onboarding P separately earned.
[KPI] Metered revenue excludes onboarding and expiry. Deck compares total revenue divided by total actual usage as metered unit price, and treats credit expiry as additional physical volume.
[Cash] Opening cash 10m; only P prepayment, Q collection and current expense cash movements.

qas.question: Find contract P earned revenue split across onboarding, consumption and expiry.
qas.answer: 4 onboarding +16 usage +4 expiry=24 million USD, with no remaining credit liability.

qas.question: Find contract Q usage revenue including the December unbilled units.
Reconcile closing Q receivable, including unconditional unbilled amount.
Determine operating profit on both contracts and shared infrastructure.
Find metered realized price per actual usage unit under the KPI definition.
Why is expired unused credit revenue not evidence of extra compute served?
qas.answer: It arises from release of a prepaid obligation upon expiry, without physical consumption; usage remains 16m for P.

qas.question: Is Q's 2.4m December amount automatically a contract asset because no invoice exists yet?
qas.answer: No. The case specifies an unconditional billing right, so it belongs to receivables.

qas.question: Can future gross retention of these customers be estimated from credit expiry?
qas.answer: No. Renewals, future usage commitments and cancellation behavior are absent.

assumptions: USD million; million barrels. Fictional production sharing contract. Toy government receives royalty off gross; cost oil limited to 60% post-royalty revenue and eligible unrecovered cost; profit oil split 55% government/45% contractor. Contractor revenue = cost oil + contractor profit oil; all physical oil sold.

evidence.text: [Production] Gross annual production 4m barrels sold at $70/barrel. Royalty 10% gross value allocated to government before cost/profit oil. No price adjustment.
[Cost pool] Opening eligible unrecovered costs 60m, current qualifying costs 110m; nonqualifying admin cost 10m excluded from recovery but expensed. No prior adjustment.
[PSC] Cost oil = lesser of eligible pool and 60% of post-royalty gross revenue. Remaining profit oil split 55% government, 45% contractor. No other taxes or fees in toy.

[Accounting] Current qualifying costs 110 expensed in P&L; historical unrecovered balance is contractual tracking only, not asset in toy. Contractor recognizes its allocated proceeds as revenue. All cash settled.
[Cash] Current 110 qualifying and 10 admin paid; no current capex or debt. Opening contractor cash 30m.
[Deck] Operator reports gross 280m as its revenue and assumes all 170m eligible cost is recovered immediately.
[Risk] Future production, oil price and eligible future cost unknown.

qas.question: Find post-royalty value available for cost and profit oil.
Find allowed cost-oil recovery under the annual ceiling.
qas.answer: Eligible pool 170; ceiling 252×.60=151.2, so recovery 151.2 million USD.

qas.question: Find closing unrecovered contractual cost pool.
Find contractor profit-oil share in money terms.
Find contractor's earned revenue and its current-year operating result; report operating result.
Why is gross field revenue 280 not the contractor's revenue?
qas.answer: Royalty and government profit-oil allocation belong to government; only cost recovery and contractor profit share belong to contractor.

qas.question: Can closing unrecovered cost pool 18.8 be booked as an asset under the stated policy?
qas.answer: No. The case explicitly treats it as contractual tracking, not a recognized asset; recovery depends on future ceiling and eligible production.

qas.question: Can the date when the 18.8 pool will be fully recovered be established?
qas.answer: No. Future production, price and additional eligible costs determine future cost-oil headroom.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional housing developer Elm Pier. Toy revenue recognized upon individual unit handover, deposits create contract liability. VAT collected as agent, excluded from sales and margin. Each unit identical cost.

evidence.text: [Sales ledger] 100 apartments contracted at base price 2m each plus VAT 10%; all buyers paid 30% of base and proportionate VAT at signing. 60 apartments handed over by year-end; buyers of handed units pay remaining 70% plus VAT.

[Inventory] Completed 100 units cost 140m, all qualifying inventory cost, no opening inventory beyond these units; unit cost 1.4m. Cash construction payments 120m this year; 20m payable at closing, no opening AP.
[Handover] Only the 60 handed units qualify for sales; remaining 40 not transferred. No cancellations or refunds.
[Tax cash] All VAT collected in period remains payable except 10m remitted. No input VAT credit in toy; no corporate tax.
[Expense] Selling/admin cash expense 12m, debt interest cash/expense 8m. No other financing, opening cash 80m.
[Deck] Sales shows 200m contracted base as revenue, treats all presale cash including VAT as earned revenue, and expenses full 140 inventory cost.
[Note] No future handover schedule, lender covenant or additional construction budget.

qas.question: Find recognized base property sales revenue after the handover cut-off.
Calculate closing contract liability for the 40 unhanded apartments, excluding VAT.
Find closing unsold/untransferred inventory at cost.
Reconcile current VAT liability from all customer VAT receipts and remittance.
qas.answer: Base cash=100×2×.3+60×2×.7=144; VAT collected 14.4; liability 4.4 million USD.

qas.question: Determine profit before tax with matched transferred unit cost.
Explain why expensing the full 140m inventory cost is inconsistent with the 60 handovers.
qas.answer: Only transferred apartments enter COGS (84m); cost of 40 units remains inventory 56m. Cash construction 120 is a separate payment measure.

qas.question: Should signing deposits on future handovers be presented as current sales merely because customers have paid?
qas.answer: No. The toy requires control transfer at handover; advance cash creates a service/delivery obligation, VAT is separate.

qas.question: Can next year's realized profit be projected exactly using the remaining 40 apartments?
qas.answer: No. Handover timing, cancellations, later selling costs and other income/expense are not specified.

assumptions: USD million; million units. Fictional private fund Alder Current. Toy side pocket allocated exclusively to investors present before segregation; redemption from liquid sleeve only. No fee or tax; separate unit registers.

evidence.text: [Opening NAV] Total 200m; liquid assets net 160m, illiquid holding 40m. Existing 20m units before segregation, 8m held by investor X, 12m by Y.
[Segregation] Side pocket created at carrying 40m, issues 20m side-pocket units to existing investors pro rata. Liquid sleeve retains 20m units, NAV 160m. No asset movement outside fund.
[Subscription] New investor Z contributes 40m into liquid sleeve immediately at NAV/unit $8; receives 5m liquid units only. No side-pocket rights.
[Revaluation] After subscription, liquid sleeve gains 25m, side pocket loss 10m. Before redemption no other flows.
[Redemption] X redeems 4m liquid units at current liquid NAV per unit; retains all side-pocket units. Payment made in cash, no gate or charge.
[Presentation] Fund manager divides combined NAV by liquid units and offers Z a share of side pocket; treats side-pocket loss as liability to Z.
[Disclosure] No later realization or exit values for illiquid holding.

qas.question: Find liquid NAV immediately after subscription and before investment gains.
Calculate liquid sleeve NAV/unit after gains and before X's redemption.
Find X's cash redemption on four million liquid units.
qas.answer: Liquid sleeve NAV before redemption = 160 + 40 + 25 = 225m; liquid units = 20 + 5 = 25m. Redemption price = 225/25 = $9/unit. X redeems 4m liquid units for 36 million USD; side-pocket units are excluded.

qas.question: Find side-pocket NAV attributable to X after revaluation.
Reconcile total fund NAV after X's liquid redemption, including the separate side pocket.
Why is combined NAV divided by liquid units the wrong redemption price?
qas.answer: Side pocket rights belong to original holders on a distinct register; liquid redeemers only claim liquid NAV. Including it misallocates illiquid value.

qas.question: Does Z bear any direct loss from the 10m side-pocket write-down?
qas.answer: No. Z subscribes only to liquid sleeve and receives no side-pocket units.

qas.question: Can the amount or timing of future side-pocket cash distribution be determined?
qas.answer: No. Current marked NAV is not realized cash; no binding exit or future recovery schedule exists.
